The statement signals a still-strong labor market and solid activity, but emphasizes below-target inflation and a patient policy stance. Viewed through a Taylor-rule lens (as the Fed often resembles in practice), inflation running under 2% with unemployment near its natural rate warrants holding rates steady rather than tightening. Anchored expectations and “inflation forecast targeting” à la Svensson support patience when realized inflation undershoots. The muted inflation response despite low unemployment is consistent with a flatter Phillips curve and sticky-information dynamics (Mankiw and Reis), reinforcing a cautious bias. Credibility built since the Volcker era mitigates time-consistency/inflation-bias concerns (Barro-Gordon), and Orphanides’ real-time measurement cautions also justify avoiding overreaction. The IOER adjustment is a technical move to keep the funds rate within the target range. Net tone: moderately positive on growth and jobs, tempered by disinflationary readings and a dovish, wait-and-see stance.
